data.title: Florida Dermatology Group Hit by Cyberattack, Social Security Numbers, Financial Details, and Medical Records of 85,585 Patients at Risk
data.description:
The personal, financial and medical records of tens of thousands of patients may be in the hands of hackers after a cyberattack on a Florida skin care practice.

The Orlando-based Mid Florida Dermatology & Plastic Surgery says an unauthorized party may have copied information from its systems between March 26th and March 30th.

The practice, which runs 33 offices across central Florida, reported the breach to the US Department of Health and Human Services on May 1st as affecting roughly 85,585 people, reports Claim Depot.

The ransomware group Qilin claimed responsibility for the attack on a dark web post on April 25th.

The company says it spotted unusual activity on March 30th and finished reviewing the affected files on August 31st.

The exposed information varies by person but may include names, addresses, dates of birth, Social Security numbers, driver’s license numbers, passport numbers and Medicare numbers.

Financial account numbers, account access information, health insurance details and medical information may also be involved.

Mid Florida Dermatology is mailing notice letters to affected patients and says anyone who doesn’t get one can call its assistance line at 1-877-344-1677 to check whether they were impacted.

The practice is urging patients to review account statements, explanation of benefits forms and credit reports for suspicious activity.

data.title: Brooklyn Prosecutors Seize 112 Servers in Crypto Investment Scam Targeting Russian Community in US
data.description:
Brooklyn prosecutors are dismantling the infrastructure of a major cryptocurrency investment scam that targeted Russian speakers across the United States.

The Brooklyn District Attorney’s Virtual Currency Unit says it seized and disrupted 241 web domains and 112 servers in one of the largest local cyber enforcement actions.

“The operation seized and disrupted not only 241 scam cryptocurrency investment domains but, more significantly, a large cluster of over 100 cloud-based servers hosted by Eastern European and American companies, depriving the scammers of access to the data that populates the domains, victim information, and their operational software.”

The scam ran for more than three years and relied on Russian-language Facebook ads plus Russian-speaking advisors to lure victims into fake investment platforms.

Victims transferred cryptocurrency to the sites and were later told they had to shell out funds to cover additional fees and taxes before they could make a withdrawal. The scammers also ran a crypto recovery scheme, duping victims into believing their digital assets were stolen and promising that the coins would be recovered.

Tens of millions of dollars were lost, with some victims losing life savings. About $300,000 has been recovered so far, and the district attorney’s office is working to claw back more.

Brooklyn District Attorney Eric Gonzalez emphasizes the operation’s impact on victims.

“When scammers halfway around the world target Brooklyn residents, they should know they are not beyond our reach. These criminals stole many millions of dollars from Russian-speaking victims through an elaborate investment scheme, then tried to exploit them again with false promises to recover their money.”

The office had previously seized or disrupted more than 400 related domains tied to cryptocurrency investment fraud.

data.title: Kansas CEO Masterminds $1,000,000,0000 Medicare Fraud, Sentenced to 19 Years Behind Bars
data.description:
Federal prosecutors have secured a 19-year prison sentence against a Kansas businessman who operated an online platform that generated false medical orders to defraud Medicare.

Brett Blackman, 43, of Johnson County, Kansas, was convicted after a 23-day trial on charges including wire fraud, conspiracy to pay and receive kickbacks, and conspiracy to defraud the United States and to make false statements in connection with health care matters, says the U.S. Department of Justice.

Blackman owned HealthSplash, which acquired the DMERx platform in 2017, and his co-defendant Gary Cox was sentenced to 15 years in December 2025.

The platform connected suppliers with doctors who signed orders for unneeded braces without examining patients. The DME suppliers and pharmacies that paid illegal kickbacks for the orders submitted more than $1 billion in claims to Medicare and other insurers, which paid out more than $450 million. Blackman and his co-conspirators hid the scheme through sham contracts and altered doctors’ orders to evade Medicare audits, including by removing references to telemedicine.

The scheme resulted in fraudulent Medicare billing for orthotic braces for more than 346,000 beneficiaries. Medicare was billed for an average of four braces per beneficiary. In more than 1,200 cases, beneficiaries received at least 21 orthotics prescribed through Blackman’s DMERx platform.

Says Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division,

“The Department of Justice and our agency partners dismantled one of the largest telemedicine fraud schemes ever, and yesterday’s lengthy prison sentence holds the orchestrator of that scheme accountable.”

data.title: Berkshire Hathaway Pours Another $330,000,000 Into Software Company As Shares Surge 41%
data.description:
Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.A/BRK/B) has agreed to pour another $330 million into Milan-based software operator Bending Spoons (BSP).

The firm will buy 10 million newly issued ordinary shares at $33 apiece in a private placement, reports 24/7 Wall St.

The latest outlay builds on a $600 million investment at the July initial public offering, bringing Berkshire’s combined commitment near $930 million at purchase prices and taking its ownership to about a 4% stake, says Bending Spoons.

Says co-founder and chief executive Luca Ferrari,

“For decades now, Berkshire Hathaway has been among the finest and most respected capital allocators in the world, and is a longstanding inspiration for Bending Spoons.”

Bending Spoons acquires and runs mature software and internet businesses such as Airtable, AOL, Brightcove, Eventbrite, Evernote, Tractive, Vimeo and WeTransfer.

Shares closed at $53.46 on Thursday after jumping 41.2% from the prior session’s price of $37.86, leaving the stock well above the $33 price Berkshire locked in.

Says Francesco Patarnello, Bending Spoons Head of Business Acquisitions and co-founder,

“Bending Spoons continuously evaluates M&A opportunities, and our pipeline remains strong. We believe Berkshire Hathaway’s investment reflects confidence in our team and Platform and will further enhance our financial flexibility and ability to pursue attractive acquisitions as part of our broader financing strategy.”

The placement price was fixed before the rally, so buyers at the close paid a steep premium to Berkshire’s entry.

The private placement remains subject to standard closing conditions, with closing expected in the fourth quarter.

Berkshire’s Class B shares rose about 1% after the announcement.

data.title: Billionaire Paul Tudor Jones Warns 2027 Will Be ‘Really, Really Challenging’ for Stocks – Here’s Why
data.description:
Billionaire hedge fund manager Paul Tudor Jones is warning that next year could be a brutal one for the stock market.

Speaking on CNBC’s Squawk Box, the founder and chief investment officer of Tudor Investment says a flood of new stock supply from big tech initial public offerings (IPOs) is set to weigh on prices.

Jones says corporate buybacks and mergers and acquisitions have shrunk the supply of shares for most of the four-year bull market, but that tide is now turning.

He points to major offerings ahead from AI firms Anthropic and OpenAI, one just finished for SpaceX and likely secondary offerings from companies raising money for the AI build-out.

Says Jones,

“2027 is going to be really, really challenging for the stock market. You’ve probably got the most negative flow picture for the U.S. stock market that we’ve had, say, since 2002.”

Jones again compares today’s market to 1999, about a year before the dot-com bubble burst.

He also sees the ballooning US fiscal deficit as a danger for stocks.

Says Jones,

“We’re never going to fix these deficits until the market makes us to. It’s going to be just like 2008 and TARP [Troubled Asset Relief Program]. So that’s the reality. No politician is going to voluntarily raise taxes or cut spending. They’re going to be forced to.”

Jones puts the odds that markets are now at that tipping point at 60-40.

He is also long oil and says prices could rally another $20 to $25 after the midterms, a scenario he says the stock market will “hate.”

Jones says the late 1990s and early 2000s were the easiest years to be short because unlocks kept adding supply to the market.

Says Jones,

“I’ll be short the whole year. There just – there’s little value.”

data.title: Standard Chartered Rolls Out First Bank-Integrated Bitcoin and Ethereum Trading for Affluent UAE Clients
data.description:
Standard Chartered is introducing a cryptocurrency trading solution that lets its wealthy UAE clients buy and sell Bitcoin and Ethereum directly through their existing bank accounts in a closed-loop system with institutional custody.

The bank says this marks a global first for the institution and the UAE’s first such offering by an international bank, regulated by the Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (VARA).

Eligible affluent clients can execute trades within the bank’s ecosystem where Standard Chartered handles custody and settlement to reduce third-party risks through collaboration with its wealth and corporate businesses plus SC Ventures-backed Zodia Markets.

The service launches first for Professional Investor clients in the UAE with expansion planned to other markets later and builds on the bank’s existing crypto access through ETFs, structured products and OTC derivatives.

Samir Subberwal, Global Head of Wealth Solutions at the bank, highlights growing client interest in digital assets.

“With digital assets moving into mainstream wealth conversations, clients are increasingly looking not only for access, but also for the security, trust and confidence that comes from investing through a regulated and trusted institution.”

Rola Abu Manneh, CEO for UAE, Middle East and Pakistan at Standard Chartered, notes the strategic fit with the region.

“We are proud to be the first international bank in the UAE to launch a cryptocurrency trading offering. The UAE was a natural choice for this launch, given the country’s forward-looking approach to innovation, strong regulatory environment and growing leadership in digital assets. This also reflects the strategic importance of the UAE within our network as one of our four global wealth hubs.”

data.title: New Jersey Man Gets 16 Years in Prison, Ordered To Surrender $1,800,000 for Stealing From Bank Accounts and Cashing Stolen US Treasury Checks
data.description:
A repeat bank fraudster who sent imposters into bank branches to drain victims’ accounts and cash stolen US Treasury checks has been sentenced to more than 16 years in federal prison.

Laquan Williams, 42, of Florham Park, New Jersey, was sentenced to 200 months in prison for conspiracy to commit bank fraud and aggravated identity theft, says the US Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York.

Prosecutors say Williams ran a series of schemes between 2021 and 2024 that caused about $1.8 million in losses to financial institutions.

In one, he allegedly sent co-conspirators into banks in New York, New Jersey and Connecticut to impersonate customers, including a prominent former federal government official.

In another, prosecutors say an imposter posing as small business owners got banks to move money into look-alike accounts that Williams controlled.

He also took part in depositing stolen Treasury checks, including one for $13.9 million at a Massachusetts bank, with intended losses topping $30 million, according to prosecutors.

When he was arrested in May of 2024, authorities say they found more than 1,000 stolen or altered checks, 571 counterfeit IDs, an ID card press, two pistols and ammunition.

Williams committed the crimes while on federal supervised release after a 64-month sentence in 2018 for a similar bank fraud scheme.

Says US Attorney Jamie McDonald,

“Laquan Williams is a bank fraudster who has stolen millions of dollars from Americans by engaging in identity theft and bank fraud. For nearly two decades, Williams has been stealing money from innocent bank customers with forged checks, counterfeit identification cards, and stolen personal identifying information. Today’s prison sentence protects New Yorkers and should be a reminder that we and our law enforcement partners will aggressively pursue serial fraudsters and hold them accountable.”

Williams was also ordered to forfeit about $1.8 million and pay restitution.

data.title: AI Weaponized in 84% of Ransomware Attacks, According to a New Survey
data.description:
Victims say artificial intelligence was weaponized in the vast majority of recent ransomware attacks on their organizations, according to a new survey.

In its 2026 Ransomware Risk Report, cybersecurity company Semperis says found AI was involved in 84% of the incidents experienced by the IT and security professionals polled across nine countries.

The survey, limited to organizations hit by ransomware in the past year, also showed 40% of attacks included psychological or physical threats against employees and their families, with attackers following through in 53% of those cases.

Identity systems were targeted in 87% of the incidents, while nearly 70% of victims faced multiple attacks and 31% made multiple ransom payments.

Says Chris Inglis, a former U.S. national cyber director and Semperis strategic adviser,

“Holding you at physical risk is the latest phenomenon because we’ve covered most of the other risks.”

Says Mickey Bresman, Semperis CEO,

“The bad guys are always evolving their tactics. When the initial wave of ransomware attacks began, most focused on data encryption. Then, after data backup and recovery systems started gaining traction and enabling companies to resist ransom demands, we saw the double extortion: encryption coupled with data theft and threats to expose or sell that data. So, it makes sense that we’ll continue to see attackers trying to find more ways to make victims pay.”

Semperis is an identity-driven cyber resilience and crisis response company.

data.title: JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo and Six Other Banks Debanked Customers Over Political and Religious Beliefs, Federal Regulator Finds
data.description:
Nine of the largest banks in the US had policies that cut off or limited service to Americans over their political or religious beliefs and lawful businesses, according to a federal regulator.

All nine banks had such policies between 2020 and September of 2025, says the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC).

The banks are JPMorgan Chase Bank, Bank of America, Citibank, Wells Fargo Bank, U.S. Bank, Capital One, PNC Bank, TD Bank and BMO Bank.

The OCC’s report says broad reputation risk policies with no clear standards disadvantaged customers based on their political, religious or social views.

The regulator also found the banks restricted entire industries, including oil and gas exploration, coal mining, firearms, detention facilities, tobacco and digital assets.

In one example, the report says a bank-owned payment processor closed the account of a merchant selling Make America Great Again merchandise in February of 2021.

In another, a bank declined to serve a public education organization whose political arm endorsed only Democratic candidates.

The OCC reviewed nearly 100,000 complaints and about 50,000 documents totaling roughly 420,000 pages from the banks.

Says Comptroller of the Currency Jonathan V. Gould,

“Today’s report provides irrefutable evidence that the nation’s largest banks have denied, debanked and discriminated against customers and lawful businesses.”

Says Gould,

“Notwithstanding certain efforts by the largest banks to rein in these practices, I am not confident that they will be enough. Accordingly, the OCC will be assessing further changes to the regulatory and supervisory framework applicable to the largest banks to reduce the likelihood of these harmful practices recurring in the future.”

data.title: ‘Big Short’ Investor Michael Burry Hints Stocks Could Peak Within Nine Months, Funnels Bearish Bets Into Nasdaq and Chip Stocks ETF
data.description:
The investor who famously called the 2008 housing crash is hinting that US stocks could hit a major peak within the next nine months.

Michael Burry has consolidated nearly all of his bearish exposure into put options on the Nasdaq-100 index (NDX) and the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH), reports 24/7 Wall St.

Burry disclosed the moves on his Cassandra Unchained Substack earlier this week.

A put option is a financial contract that gives the buyer the right, but not the obligation, to sell an underlying asset at a set price (strike price) by a specific expiration date. The value of a put option goes up when the market price of the underlying asset drops below the strike price

His Nasdaq-100 puts expire in April of 2027, while his semiconductor ETF puts run through June of 2027.

Burry says he is keeping his longer-dated puts on Palantir Technologies (PLTR) and Oracle (ORCL) but closing out his other bearish positions.

The semiconductor ETF has surged more than 67% so far this year, led by Nvidia (NVDA), Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) and AMD (AMD), which together make up 34.5% of its holdings.

AMD alone is up more than 170% in 2026, while TSM has gained 43% and Nvidia has climbed 20%.

Burry previously closed his December 2026 Nvidia puts as time decay ate into the position.

Nine months from October also stretches into July of 2027, past both reported expiration dates, meaning a late peak could fit Burry’s forecast but arrive too late for his contracts.

The report notes Burry has not disclosed position sizes or premiums paid, leaving it unclear whether his overall bearish bet has actually grown.
